title: Partial Clones
description: Use Git partial clones to download history without all file contents, saving disk space while preserving bisect and log capabilities.

data.text: Git partial clones (--filter) download the full commit history but omit file contents. When you need a file, Git downloads it on demand from the remote. This gives you full history access (bisect, log, blame) while dramatically reducing disk usage for repositories with large files.
Use git clone --filter=<spec> to control which objects are downloaded. The most useful filter is blob:none, which downloads all commits and trees but omits all file contents (blobs).

data.title: Clone with blob:none filter
data.code:
# Partial clone: full history, no file contents
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/example/project.git

# The repository has:
# - All commits and trees (for bisect, log, blame)
# - No file contents (blobs) until you request them

# Checkout a file — Git downloads it on demand
git switch main
git checkout src/app/Program.cs

# Verify the file is present
ls src/app/Program.cs

rows: Default partial clone; download files on demand
Include small files, download large files on demand
Minimal clone for commit graph only

items: **Requires modern server**: The remote must support the Git partial clone protocol (GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket support it)
**Network dependency**: Accessing uncached files requires a network connection
**Slower file access**: First access to a file downloads it, adding latency
**Not supported everywhere**: Older Git clients and some tools do not support partial clones

data.title: Partial clones require a compatible server
data.text: The remote server must support the Git partial clone protocol. GitHub and GitLab support it. Self-hosted Git servers may require Git 2.19+ and specific configuration.

Partial clones preserve the full history, so you can bisect and log across all commits. Shallow clones truncate history, making bisect impossible for older commits. Use partial clones when you need history but not all files.

data.title: Compare shallow and partial clones
data.code:
# Shallow clone: last 10 commits, all files
git clone --depth 10 https://github.com/example/project.git

# Partial clone: all commits, no files
git clone --filter=blob:none https://github.com/example/project.git

# Partial clone with size limit: all commits, files under 100KB
git clone --filter=blob:limit=100k https://github.com/example/project.git

# Use case:
# - Shallow: CI builds that only need the latest code
# - Partial: debugging that needs full history but not large assets

data.text: If you need all files in a partial clone, use git checkout . or git restore . to download all missing blobs. Git fetches them from the remote in the background.

data.title: Download all missing files
data.code:
# After partial clone, download all files
git checkout .

# Or for a specific directory
git checkout -- src/

# Verify all files are present
git ls-files | wc -l

# Check disk usage
du -sh .git

items.question: Can I push from a partial clone?
items.answer: Yes. Partial clones support push because they have the full history. Only file contents are missing, and those are not needed for push.

items.question: Does partial clone work with Git LFS?
items.answer: Yes. Partial clones and Git LFS can be combined. Git LFS handles large binary files; partial clones handle the remaining history optimization.

items.question: Can I use partial clone with existing repositories?
items.answer: Partial clone is a clone-time option. For existing repositories, use git sparse-checkout or git lfs migrate import to reduce disk usage.

items.question: Does GitHub support partial clones?
items.answer: Yes. GitHub supports partial clones for HTTPS and SSH remotes. Use --filter=blob:none when cloning from GitHub.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: git clone --filter=blob:none downloads full history but no file contents
Files download on demand when you checkout or access them
Partial clones preserve bisect and log capabilities
Requires a compatible server (GitHub, GitLab support it)
Combine with sparse checkout for maximum disk savings
